architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.evaluated_over: the selectable experiment cards of this arm
decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Run at least two independent repeats and accept the combined low-drift outcome if SI_15_60 is below 3.80% in each repeat. This is below half the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction for reactive mass fraction 0.8000 and supports H-RESIN over H-CORE, while remaining consistent with H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: The primary observable is a direct isothermal hold measurement and does not depend on a shared thermal-response shape or state-transfer regularity. Therefore it is interpretable for the selected AC1920/TK100 composition as a formulation-level rheological result. The candidate is nevertheless marked modified_chemistry_unvalidated relative to the measured unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI family, so no thermal-shape transfer or broader chemistry-general claim is justified.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: If SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61% in the matched 15-60 min window, H-RESIN is falsified in favor of the H-CORE linear-dilution account. If SI_15_60 is below 3.80%, H-CORE is falsified at the stated 2.00% discrimination resolution. Results between 3.80% and 7.61%, or repeats that span these thresholds, are non-decisive. No result from this dual-axis composition separates H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run a compositionally matched 120 C M-HOLD-120 acrylic-only experiment with 15% AC1920, 0% TK100, the corresponding reactive-mass-fraction-specific linear-dilution benchmark, and the same recorded preparation and repeat protocol.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, measured at 120 C over 15-60 min.
judge_normalized.rationale: This experiment directly measures the declared failure mode, thermal-hold viscosity drift, rather than inferring it from a temperature sweep or one-point anchor. S1C41 uses the smallest total modifier burden among the tied dual-axis top cards while retaining both independently supported modifier regions. The result can distinguish combined low drift from reactive-core linear dilution, but cannot establish molecular mechanism or minor-tackifier-specific causality.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator in selecting S1C41::M-HOLD-120, including their minimum-sufficient-intervention tie-break among the five deterministic top cards. I incorporated the Skeptic's objection by explicitly leaving H-RESIN and H-DUAL entangled and limiting interpretation to the combined formulation-level hold response. The advisory chemistry audit does not mark this direct-hold experiment inadmissible, although it marks the candidate chemistry as unvalidated for shared-shape transfer.

action_requests.name: get_chemistry_audited_rheology_summary
action_requests.reason: Mandatory upstream evidence: candidate and experiment ranking is inadmissible until the chemistry provenance, local rheological regularities, state-shift evidence, thermal-shape support and original hold contrasts are audited and loaded.

action_requests.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
action_requests.reason: Needed to compare candidate experiment cards against the evidence-derived acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like axes, the E2 reactive-core anchor and the historical claim boundary without treating the hypothesis as a discovered optimum.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The local rheological regularities were measured in the original PUR reactive-core formulation family represented by E1-E5, including the local acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like modifier axes. The intended experiment would remain inside that original PUR modifier family rather than introduce a chemistry-changing modifier such as AC1920 or TK100; exact support must nevertheless be confirmed by the audited chemistry summary before using any shared-shape or state-transfer regularity.
planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged 120 C melt residence (thermal-hold drift)
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original 120 C matched-window hold shows SI_15_60 = 51.54% for E5, compared with 9.51% for E1, establishing substantial time-dependent viscosity growth in the local system.
planner.least_resolved_justification: The local hold evidence contains only two original formulations, E1 and E5, with four time points over 15-90 min and no follow-up mean profiles or matched modifier-axis comparisons. In contrast, temperature response has six measured temperatures and multiple runs, while realized viscosity level is at least characterized descriptively, although E2 shows a large 2.80-3.57x repeat spread and the viscosity unit remains unknown.
measurement_requirements: Measure a matched-window 120 C thermal hold at 15, 30, 45 and 60 min with at least two independent repeats, and report SI_15_60 directly for the candidate.

Record the formulation composition, reactive mass fraction, preparation history and measurement state so the observed drift can be compared with the linear-dilution prediction without conflating chemistry with process-state variation.
Use the measured hold trajectory, not an extrapolated temperature-response model, as the primary discriminator between core-only dilution and superlinear resin suppression.

If distinguishing the dual-axis hypothesis is intended, include a compositionally matched acrylic-only comparison or otherwise provide evidence that the low-drift result cannot be attributed to the acrylic-like axis alone.
planner.scientific_question: At matched reactive mass fraction and a 120 C residence window, does a resin-modified candidate produce drift consistent with linear reactive-core dilution, or drift substantially below that prediction as required by resin-modification suppression; if the candidate has a nonzero minor-tackifier-like axis, is the low-drift response specific to that axis rather than obtainable from an acrylic-like modifier alone?

planner_action_requests_after_forcing.name: get_chemistry_audited_rheology_summary
planner_action_requests_after_forcing.reason: Mandatory upstream evidence: candidate and experiment ranking is inadmissible until the chemistry provenance, local rheological regularities, state-shift evidence, thermal-shape support and original hold contrasts are audited and loaded.

planner_action_requests_after_forcing.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
planner_action_requests_after_forcing.reason: Needed to compare candidate experiment cards against the evidence-derived acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like axes, the E2 reactive-core anchor and the historical claim boundary without treating the hypothesis as a discovered optimum.

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: The primary observable is matched-window 120 C thermal-hold drift measured directly, without reconstructing viscosity from the shared thermal-response shape. Therefore it remains scientifically admissible even though AC1920/TK100 chemistry is outside the validated shared-shape family. The chemistry audit limits shape-transfer claims but does not invalidate this direct drift measurement.
hypotheses_not_separated: H-RESIN versus H-DUAL; both predict the same low-drift outcome for this dual-axis composition

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 remains below 3.80% across at least two repeats, the result supports H-RESIN over H-CORE because drift is below half the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction. It is also consistent with H-DUAL, but cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified and the result supports the H-CORE linear-dilution account. If drift is below 3.80%, H-CORE is falsified. These thresholds exceed the 2.00% discrimination resolution.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result between 3.80% and 7.61%, or one with repeat-to-repeat variation spanning these thresholds, is ambiguous at the declared resolution and does not decisively adjudicate H-CORE versus the low-drift hypotheses. H-RESIN versus H-DUAL remains unresolved in all cases without an acrylic-only comparison.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It is genuinely VOI-tied, but uses a larger 17.5% acrylic-like modifier burden than the minimum sufficient 15% choice.
It is genuinely VOI-tied, but uses a larger 20% acrylic-like modifier burden and therefore a larger departure from the local reactive core.
It is genuinely VOI-tied, but uses a larger 22.5% acrylic-like modifier burden without additional hypothesis discrimination.
It is genuinely VOI-tied, but uses the largest 25% acrylic-like modifier burden in the supported region and offers no additional direct-hold discrimination.
Its 2.5% TK100 level lies below the repeatedly supported minor-resin cluster and incurs nonzero extrapolation risk, lowering VOI relative to S1C41.

proposer.reasoning: The failure mode is directly isothermal time-dependent drift, so M-HOLD-120 is preferable to inferred anchor or temperature-sweep observables. S1C41 has the highest VOI score, ties four other cards, directly tests the least-resolved coordinate, separates the linear-dilution hypothesis from the low-drift alternatives, and uses the smallest dual-axis intervention within the supported composition regions. The advisory chemistry audit does not undermine the direct drift observable.
proposer.tie_break_justification: S1C41 uses the smallest total modifier burden in the tied set while remaining inside both externally supported intervention regions: 15% acrylic-like AC1920 and 5% minor-tackifier-like TK100. It is therefore the minimum sufficient dual-axis intervention and minimizes departure from the characterized reactive core while retaining the same direct-hold hypothesis discrimination.

residual_decision_risk: The dual-axis design confounds AC1920, TK100, their interaction, and reactive-mass-fraction dilution.
H-RESIN and H-DUAL remain entangled without a compositionally matched acrylic-only comparison.
M-HOLD-120 does not control process state, and two repeats may produce ambiguous or variable threshold classification.

The candidate is marked modified_chemistry_unvalidated with no verified shared-shape transfer; the direct hold remains interpretable, but no unmodified-family thermal-shape or state-transfer claim is justified.
The experiment cannot establish the molecular encounter-frequency explanation or distinct rheological-coordinate mechanism.
The tied top set reflects score indifference among five dual-axis cards; the preference for S1C41 is a scientific minimum-sufficient-intervention tie-break, not a VOI advantage.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is valid: S1C41 changes AC1920 and TK100 simultaneously, so H-RESIN and H-DUAL make the same low-drift prediction and the experiment cannot establish that suppression specifically requires the minor-tackifier-like axis. Nevertheless, M-HOLD-120 remains the direct measurement most relevant to the declared failure mode and can still distinguish the combined low-drift outcome from H-CORE. The result must therefore be interpreted as evidence about this combined intervention versus the linear-dilution account, not as separation of H-RESIN from H-DUAL or proof of axis-specific mechanism. An acrylic-only matched hold is required for that additional attribution.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The proposal is in the tied deterministic top set. No tested scaling of any weight term from 0.5 to 1.5 changes the tied top set: top_experiment_set_stability is 1.0, intervention_family_stability is 1.0, and measurement_plan_stability is 1.0. The base margin to the first strictly lower experiment is 0.004583. The recommendation_flip_boundary reports no flip for any weight term across the full sweep. These perturbations are scientifically defensible as a sensitivity check, but the resulting stability is decision stability of the transparent VOI score, not confidence or evidence that the experiment is scientifically correct.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: The primary observable stays within the admissible measurement domain because M-HOLD-120 directly measures 120 C matched-window drift and does not reuse the unmodified-family shared thermal-response shape. The candidate itself remains outside the validated unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI chemistry support: AC1920/TK100 is marked modified_chemistry_unvalidated with no verified shape transfer. Direct modified-composition temperature sweeps would be required before making shared-shape or state-transfer claims.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The protocol records eta at 15, 30, 45 and 60 minutes and reports SI_15_60 directly, so it can produce values below 3.80% or at or above 7.61%. These cutoffs differ by more than the declared 2.00% resolution. The uncontrolled process state and minimum of only two independent repeats can instead yield an ambiguous or highly variable result, but they do not make the criterion impossible to meet.
leakage_findings: No reliance on an unmeasured target outcome or validation-formulation identity is evident; the candidate rationale uses pre-result evidence and the chemistry audit.
The molecular encounter-frequency and different-rheological-coordinate explanations are stronger than what M-HOLD-120 can establish.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low SI_15_60 could support H-RESIN or H-DUAL, but cannot support the claimed specialization of the minor tackifier axis or distinguish the two mechanisms.
objections.objection: The selected experiment S1C41::M-HOLD-120 uses both 15% AC1920 and 5% TK100, so H-RESIN and H-DUAL make the same low-drift prediction of 3.804%. The proposer correctly states in outcome_interpretation and falsification_criterion that these hypotheses remain unresolved, but the hypotheses_separated field nevertheless lists H-DUAL as separated. The single experiment cannot establish whether suppression is a general resin effect or specifically requires the minor-tackifier-like axis.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The result may discriminate a combined low-drift outcome from H-CORE, but it cannot establish that the two axes act on different rheological coordinates or that TK100 is required.
objections.objection: The formulation changes two modifier axes simultaneously: AC1920 is 15% and TK100 is 5% in S1C41, while reactive mass fraction falls to 0.8000. Consequently, any observed drift change is attributable only to the combined intervention relative to the linear-dilution benchmark. The protocol cannot attribute suppression specifically to AC1920, TK100, their interaction, or the claimed relocation of viscosity level by the acrylic-like axis.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: No additional unsupported claim follows from the primary-observable construction; the direct drift result remains interpretable as an isothermal time-window measurement.
objections.objection: The primary observable SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 is read directly from the M-HOLD-120 protocol at 15 and 60 minutes. It does not require the fitted E_eta descriptor, a shared thermal-response shape, temperature extrapolation, or imputation. This part of the proposal survives the attack.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The direct 120 C drift result could support a phenomenological statement about this AC1920/TK100 composition, but not transferability of the shared thermal shape or a broader chemistry-independent explanation. A direct temperature sweep on the modified composition would be required for shape-transfer claims.
objections.objection: S1C41 is classified by the audit as modified_chemistry_unvalidated for resin_modified:ac1920+tk100, with no prior verified shape transfer. The proposal appropriately uses M-HOLD-120 rather than M-ANCHOR or M-SWEEP, so the primary drift observable does not reuse the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI shared thermal-response shape. However, the experiment is still outside the measured chemistry family's validated rheological support for any claims about thermal-shape transfer or general mechanism.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A threshold result could be overinterpreted as falsification of H-CORE or H-RESIN when uncontrolled preparation history or realization state produced the observed drift.
objections.objection: The numerical criteria are attainable in principle: for S1C41, H-RESIN is falsified at SI_15_60 at or above 7.61%, and H-CORE is falsified below 3.80%, with a 2.00% declared resolution and at least two repeats. However, M-HOLD-120 does not control process state, and the card assigns process_state_risk 0.75 with six missing process fields. The protocol therefore can produce a threshold-crossing result, but repeat-to-repeat variation may yield the explicitly acknowledged ambiguous interval or make attribution to chemistry unreliable.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment could justify an outcome-level comparison with the linear-dilution prediction, but not a molecular reaction pathway, encounter-frequency explanation, or independent axis-specific mechanism.
objections.objection: The rheological hold cannot establish the molecular wording in H-RESIN concerning effective concentration and encounter frequency, nor the H-DUAL claim that the axes act on different rheological coordinates. The payload's claim boundary explicitly says the E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism and that formulation-level hypotheses do not imply chain-level characterization. The selected M-HOLD-120 measures only matched-window time-dependent viscosity drift.

skeptic.recommended_change: Add a compositionally matched acrylic-only 120 C hold, with the AC1920 level held at 15% and TK100 set to zero, while recalculating its reactive-mass-fraction-specific linear-dilution benchmark. Compare its SI_15_60 with S1C41 under the same recorded preparation and hold protocol. This is required to test whether the low-drift response is specifically dependent on the minor-tackifier-like axis.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The dual-axis composition S1C41 changes AC1920 and TK100 together, and H-RESIN and H-DUAL predict the same SI_15_60 value of 3.804%. Thus the experiment cannot identify whether any low drift is a general resin effect or requires the minor-tackifier-like axis, despite the hypotheses_separated field listing H-DUAL.

tool_trace.name: get_chemistry_audited_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: Mandatory upstream evidence: candidate and experiment ranking is inadmissible until the chemistry provenance, local rheological regularities, state-shift evidence, thermal-shape support and original hold contrasts are audited and loaded.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_GJJ_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 GJJ day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. Its close agreement with the primary shared thermal shape makes it useful as a defined scale-versus-shape perturbation check, not as another nominal E1 realization.

provenance_audit.reason: E1 +P is a verified chemical perturbation: 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution was added during dehydration. It is excluded from the same-composition primary state model and exposed separately as a perturbation check.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

chemistry_applicability_audit.enforcement_note: In this condition the chemistry applicability audit is ADVISORY. Every experiment card above remains selectable, including the cards the audit marks inadmissible. Use the audit as scientific evidence and justify whatever you select.
rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

top_cards.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 3.80% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 0.8000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards.admissibility_reason: The matched-window 120 C hold observes thermal-hold drift directly and does not reuse the shared thermal-response shape, so it stays admissible outside the validated chemistry family.
top_cards.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61%. H-CORE is falsified if drift falls below 3.80%, a separation larger than the 2.00% resolution threshold. This composition carries both axes, so it cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL; an acrylic-only hold is the follow-up required for that.
